summary: Intermittent TLS handshake failures to customer DB over VPC peering (production)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent TLS handshake failures when Redwood Private deployment in the customer's VPC connects to their managed Postgres database in a peer VPC. Impact: Several production requests fail with TLS errors; customer reports ~3-5% of DB connections in the last 24h returning TLS handshake failure and causing transient errors in their app. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peered to DB VPC), prod region eu-west-1. Not observed in staging. Expected behavior: Persistent TLS connections to DB should complete the handshake and remain established. Actual behavior: TLS handshake fails intermittently with alerts from application and connection logs showing "tlsv1 alert unknown ca" or TCP RST mid-handshake in packet captures.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has Redwood Private control-plane in their VPC (10.10.0.0/16) and DB in peer VPC (10.20.0.0/16) with VPC peering established
2) Issue appears when Redwood private pods make outgoing TLS connections to DB endpoint (pg.example.internal:5432)
3) Repro is intermittent; customer reports higher incidence during DB maintenance windows and when cross-VPC traffic is routed via transit gateway
4) Packet capture on a client host during a failure shows TCP handshake then TLS ClientHello but then RST or no ServerHello
5) Restarting the Redwood private deployment pod sometimes temporarily reduces failures (works for minutes-hours)
logs: app.log: 2026-03-13T09:12:02Z ERROR db: connection failed: tls: handshake failure
pg_side: 2026-03-13T09:12:02Z LOG: connection received: host=10.10.3.22 port=56542
tcpdump snippet (customer capture): 09:12:02.123 IP 10.10.3.22.56542 > 10.20.1.12.5432: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 65535, length 511 (ClientHello)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Elena): Confirmed incident, collected customer tcpdumps, logs, VPC peering config screenshots.
Hypothesis 1 (SRE): Asymmetric routing via transit gateway causes DB to receive client IP from different path and trigger connection rejection or RST from an intermediate firewall/ACL.
Hypothesis 2 (Security): TLS SNI or certificate validation mismatch due to egress NAT altering SNI or source IP, leading DB (or network firewall) to terminate connections.
Hypothesis 3 (MTU): Path MTU or TCP segmentation with peering + transit gateway causes large ClientHello to be dropped, leading to handshake timeout and occasional RSTs.
What we checked: VPC peering routes (customer shared routing table screenshots), transit-gateway attachments, security group and NACL rules, route propagation, and customer's firewall logs.

Findings: Customer is using a transit gateway between VPCs for routing to DB VPC for policy reasons. Transit gateway has an inline third-party firewall appliance that shows DROP entries aligned with the timestamps. Firewall logs indicate packets flagged as 'SYN-Fragment' or 'invalid TLS' for a subset of connections.

resolution_notes: Workaround applied: Customer added firewall bypass (skip DPI) for peered subnets between Redwood private deployment and DB VPC. This immediately reduced TLS handshake failures from ~3-5% to <0.1%. Root cause appears to be a DPI/signature update on the customer's transit-gateway-attached firewall appliance that falsely flagged certain TLS ClientHello patterns as invalid and RSTed sessions. Next steps: 1) Customer to work with firewall vendor on permanent rule update and obtain signed vendor fix; 2) Redwood will document recommended firewall bypass in 'Private VPC Peering Runbook' and add guidance to support checklist for future private deployments; 3) Follow-up ticket INT-4512 created to add automated validation for transit-gateway DPI appliances in onboarding checks. Customer confirmed workaround is acceptable for now and will keep ticket open until vendor remediation is complete.
resolution_status: Workaround in place; pending vendor remediation
